verses.text: Solomon finished building the LORD's temple and the royal palace, and he had done everything he wanted to do.
Then the LORD appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

The LORD said to him, "I have heard your prayer and the request you made to me. I have made this temple you built holy, and I have put my name there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there.
As for you, if you live before me as your father David did, with an honest heart and doing what is right, and if you do everything I command and keep my laws and rules,
then I will make your royal throne over Israel last forever. I promised this to your father David when I said, 'You will always have a descendant on the throne of Israel.'
But if you or your children turn away from me and do not keep the commands and laws I have given you, and if you go and serve other gods and worship them,
then I will remove Israel from the land I have given them. I will reject this temple I have made holy for my name. Israel will become a joke and an insult among all the nations.
This temple is so great now, but everyone who passes by will be shocked and will whistle in surprise. They will ask, 'Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?'

And people will answer, 'Because they left the LORD their God, who brought their ancestors out of Egypt. They held on to other gods and worshipped and served them. That is why the LORD brought all this disaster on them.'"
It took Solomon twenty years to build the two buildings, the LORD's temple and the royal palace.
Hiram king of Tyre had given Solomon all the cedar, cypress, and gold he wanted. So King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in the land of Galilee.
But when Hiram came from Tyre to see the towns Solomon had given him, he was not pleased with them.
He said, "My brother, what kind of towns are these you have given me?" So he called that area the Land of Kabul, meaning good for nothing, and it is still called that today.
Hiram had sent the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, about four thousand kilograms.
This is the story of the forced labour King Solomon used to build the LORD's temple, his own palace, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.
Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He burned it down and killed the Canaanites who lived there. Then he gave the city as a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife.
So Solomon rebuilt Gezer. He also built Lower Beth Horon,
Baalath, and Tamar in the wilderness of his land.
He also built all his cities for storing supplies, and cities for his chariots and his horses. He built whatever he wanted to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land he ruled.
There were still people left from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. These people were not Israelites.
They were the descendants of the nations the Israelites had not been able to destroy completely. Solomon forced them to work as slaves, and they still do today.
But Solomon did not make slaves of any Israelites. They were his soldiers, his officials, his commanders, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and horsemen.
There were also five hundred and fifty chief officers in charge of Solomon's projects. They directed the people who did the work.
After Pharaoh's daughter moved from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he built the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD. He also burned incense with them in front of the LORD. So he finished the temple.
King Solomon also built a fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath, on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent his own men, sailors who knew the sea, to serve on the ships with Solomon's men.
They sailed to Ophir and brought back four hundred and twenty talents of gold, about fourteen thousand kilograms, to King Solomon.
